-- Built to mirror the exact vocabulary logic in
-- src/app/api/assistant/route.ts (GET /api/assistant), for the tenant
-- named 'LOCAL SEED - Osteria Scala' (restaurant id
-- de100000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001) on the local Supabase stack.
--
-- country/region: DISTINCT non-blank wines.country / wines.region for this
-- restaurant_id (trimmed, blank-filtered, exactly the route's `distinct()`
-- helper).
-- grape: DISTINCT non-blank wines.varietal UNION DISTINCT non-blank
-- xwines_catalog.grapes elements, joined via
-- wines.canonical_wine_id -> canonical_wines.id -> canonical_wines.xwines_wine_id
-- -> xwines_catalog.wine_id (the route's canonical_wines(xwines_wine_id)
-- embed). xwines_catalog.grapes stores each blend as ONE array element
-- ("Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Petit Verdot"), not split into individual
-- grapes -- the route reads that array as-is (no splitting), so this
-- fixture preserves the same composite strings.
--
-- WITH tenant_wines AS (
--   SELECT w.id, w.varietal, w.region, w.country, cw.xwines_wine_id
--   FROM wines w
--   LEFT JOIN canonical_wines cw ON cw.id = w.canonical_wine_id
--   WHERE w.restaurant_id = 'de100000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'
-- ),
-- grape_values AS (
--   SELECT trim(varietal) AS grape FROM tenant_wines
--   WHERE varietal IS NOT NULL AND trim(varietal) <> ''
--   UNION
--   SELECT trim(g) AS grape
--   FROM tenant_wines tw
--   JOIN xwines_catalog xc ON xc.wine_id = tw.xwines_wine_id
--   CROSS JOIN LATERAL unnest(xc.grapes) AS g
--   WHERE trim(g) <> ''
-- )
-- SELECT country/region/grape DISTINCT lists, ordered alphabetically for
-- this fixture (bestVocabularyMatch() picks the longest match irrespective
-- of array order, so alphabetising here does not change parser behaviour).
--
-- Measured 2026-09-01 against the local loopback stack
-- (postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:57322/postgres, `supabase
-- status`). Not production data. No tenant id or email appears below.
